claims.statement: For every ordinary star T=K_{1,d} with d>=12 and every p satisfying the primary eligibility conditions, the full selected favorable-leaf aggregate S(T,p) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: Only ordinary stars K_{1,d}, d>=12, with the exact x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1 guards and the original strict favorable-leaf selector.
claims.reason: Every leaf has the same deletion selector and support. Its marked graph H_v is edgeless with all vertices marked, so q_v(j)=binomial(d-1,j). The exact first descent of K_{1,d} forces k=p-1 onto the decreasing side of this binomial row; summing identical selected terms proves the claim.

limitations: The proof treats only stars with at least twelve leaves; it does not establish a cut or compression inequality when H_v has edges.
The result does not resolve the primary aggregate for general ordinary trees or mixed marked/unmarked sectors.
No external literature or computational census was used.
